runtime_boundary: Represents the local model runner and its server. Its chat window is how local execution is exercised rather than a broad conversational workspace with durable projects and connected information, so the product is curated as a runtime rather than an assistant.
model_management: Models are discovered and downloaded from Hugging Face inside the application and managed through its interface or the lms command-line tool, which also controls the daemon and server.
hardware_requirements: Documented requirements cover Apple silicon on macOS 14 or newer, x64 systems with AVX2 and ARM Snapdragon X Elite on Windows, and x64 or ARM64 on Ubuntu 20.04 or newer. Intel-based Macs are not supported and at least 4 GB of dedicated video memory is recommended on Windows.
operational_controls: Inference runtimes are selected automatically per model and can be managed and updated from a dedicated runtimes surface. The server can be started and stopped from the application or the command-line tool.
strengths: Ships llama.cpp engine variants for CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, and Metal alongside an Apple MLX engine, selecting an engine and offload parameters automatically.
Model discovery, download, and management are integrated into one interface with a command-line equivalent.
Provides a headless mode for servers and continuous-integration hosts in addition to the desktop application.
tradeoffs: The application core is proprietary; only the command-line tool and client SDKs are published under an open license.
Execution is limited to GGUF and MLX weights, and MLX is available only on Apple silicon.
Operational visibility is confined to in-application server logs, with no documented metrics endpoint.
license_note: The application and its inference core are governed by proprietary terms that grant a non-transferable license for personal and internal business use. The separately published command-line tool and client SDKs are MIT licensed, which makes the product an open wrapper over a closed operational core.
